newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes solidly at record level.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes solidly at record level.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade on Monday at a new record high above 2,700 points after floor trade caught up with gains made in IBIS electronic trade on Friday on the back of Wall Street strength.
The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares opened floor trade above 2,700 points and touched a new record high at 2,704.74 before closing at 2702.64, a gain of 0.72 percent.
The IBIS electronic trade index had already broken the 2,700 barrier on Friday after U.S. jobs data came in weaker-than-expected.

After its sharp rise at the open the DAX index traded in a narrow range around the 2,700 mark and dealers said the DAX was consolidating at the new high level. "We're looking a bit sideways at the moment," said one trader.
Shares in insurer Allianz lost some ground even though interim results posted by the company were seen as positive and generally in line with market expectations.
Utility stocks, including Veba, Viag and RWE, firmed as trading interest moved into the sector from chemicals.
"The utilities are in demand. People are switching out of chemicals which had been the high-flyer sector. Chemicals are a little bit more defensive at the higher levels," said one dealer.
Viag stocks were also spurred on by news that Allianz said might agree to sell the firm its 10 percent stake in energy group Isarwerke.
Bayerische Vereinsbank continued a climb started on Friday and hit a new year high after a banking source said Deutsche Bank appeared to have increased its stake in the rival bank.
Car manufacturer Volkswagen gained over one percent after the company denied a newspaper report that it had problems with a joint-venture in China and said it had no intention of pulling out.
